多年来我们一直把蔬菜运到南|方的市场。我开车技术不差，|但爸爸从没让我独自去过——|直到今天。今天是我的生日：|我想做什么就做什么！|我猜爸爸在给我准备惊喜，|想让我先别碍事。也许这样更好！
value.src: We’ve been taking our vegetables to the Sowth’s market for years. I’m not a bad driver, but dad never let me go there on my own until today. But today is my birthday: I can do whatever I want! I bet my dad is preparing a surprise for me and wants me to be out of his way for now. Probably just as well!

value.cn: 我在镇子附近遇到了一件怪事。|一个漂亮的姑娘向我求助。|说不定她是帮派的人。|但我还是答应帮她了，|因为我被教导要信任别人。|带她到处看看又不会有什么坏处，|对吧？
value.src: I’ve had a strange encounter near the town. A good-looking girl asked me to help her. She could be from a gang, for all I know. But I agreed to help her, anyway, for I’ve been taught to trust people. There’s no harm in showing her around, is there?

value.cn: 我在镇子附近遇到了一件怪事。|一个漂亮的姑娘向我求助。|她的举止看起来像是帮派的人，|所以我拒绝了她要送那个可|疑包裹的请求，但我就是忘不了她。|爸爸到底要告诉我什么呢？|我还是先回家吧。
value.src: I’ve had a strange encounter near the town. A good-looking girl asked me to help her. She looked and acted like she was from a gang, so I refused to deliver some suspicious-looking package for her, but I just can’t get her out of my mind. What was my father going to tell me, I wonder? I’d better be going home now.

value.cn: 爸爸到底要告诉我什么呢？|我还是先回家吧；|我在这里待得太久了。
value.src: What was my father going to tell me, I wonder? I’d better be going home now; I’ve stayed here way too long.

value.cn: 该死的匪徒！我的卡车虽然|是硬骨头，但看起来破破烂烂的。|我打败了费利克斯的手下，|但他们威胁我的样子让我很不|舒服……
我在远处就看到村庄上空的浓烟。|可怕的事情发生了：|有人杀了所有人并烧毁了村庄。|爸爸奄奄一息，但在去|世前给了我一个像是生日礼|物的东西。他最后的话是：|「找到本·斯罗特尔！」我埋|葬了死去的乡亲，回到卡车旁。|我打开盒子，发现里面是爸|爸的积蓄、一个闪闪发光像|是光盘的东西，以及一封|写着我名字的密封信件。
我在远处就看到村庄上空的浓烟。|可怕的事情发生了：|有人杀了所有人并烧毁了村庄。|没人活着告诉我是谁干的、为什么。|我敢打赌这都是费利克斯干的。|我要找到他并杀了他，|不管付出什么代价。
信上说我被收养的，|我的生父是一个叫伊万·|戈的探险家。他留给我的一|切就是我现在开的这辆卡|车和一张神秘的光盘。|伊万·戈多年前失踪，|可能已经死了。我的世界天翻地覆。|我需要时间理清这一切，|最重要的是我需要找到父亲|问个明白。但首先我要找本|·斯罗特尔谈谈。
value.src: The letter said I was adopted and my true father was an explorer, called Ivan Go. All that’s left from him is the truck I’m driving now and a mysterious CD. Ivan Go has gone missing several years ago and is probably dead by now. My world has just turned upside down. I need some time to make sense of it all and most of all, I need to find my father and ask him lots of questions. But first I have to talk to Ben Throttle.

value.cn: 原来费利克斯在这一带劫掠|已有一阵子了。他和农夫们达|成了某种协议：他们向他交|钱换取"|保护"。|这一直很有效，直到格卢霍|耶惨案发生。大多数人太怕|费利克斯了不敢反抗，|但凭我现在的武器，|我可以端了他的老巢。
我从没走过这么远的路。|我都没意识到除了我们村还有|别的村庄。不管怎样，|我总算找到了本的小屋。
老人在我身上看到了熟悉的特征，|热情地欢迎了我。|他的屋里满是奇奇怪怪的东西。|我告诉他我的经历后，|他说我父亲已经失踪二十多年了。|他发现了重要的东西，|但在确认安全之前不想告诉任何人。|本给我讲了一些关于父|亲和他研究的事。|当我把光盘给他看时，|他想起我爸有一台能读写这种|东西的机器，就像读一本书一样。|他给了我父亲家的方向。
匪徒基地成了废墟，|费利克斯夹着尾巴逃跑了。|他没杀我父亲，所以我决定|饶他一命。他可能是恶人，|但我有什么资格审判他？|毁灭格卢霍耶的那些人比费|利克斯的帮派强大得多。|那场惨案的唯一见证者是丽莎，|那个北方来的姑娘。|我得找到她，听她说出真相。
用"奇怪"|来形容父亲的住所远远不够。|那些精密的设备对我来说只|是一堆废铁，因为我不会用。|所有机器似乎都坏了。|大概是潮气穿过破损的窗|户和屋顶侵蚀了屋内的一切。|有一样东西引起了我的注意——|一个形状不寻常的护符，|是我脚下木板断裂时发现的。
value.src: The word “strange” doesn’t even begin to describe my father’s dwelling. All those sophisticated gadgets were just a heap of junk to me, for I didn’t know how to use them. All the machines seemed to be out of order. The humid air that penetrated the house through broken windows and roof is probably the reason. One thing drew my attention – a Charm of unusual shape, which I found when a board cracked underneath my feet.

value.cn: 那姑娘不像表面看起来那么简单。|她跟匪徒混在一起。|我对她有种不祥的预感。|追了她这么远，我渐渐看|清她是什么人了。
value.src: The girl is not as simple as she lets on. She’s hanging out with bandits. I have a bad feeling about her. I’ve traveled so many miles after her and I’m beginning to understand what kind of bird she is.

value.cn: 我怎么竟怀疑过这个可怜的人？|她当时又害怕又无助。|丽莎告诉了我阿克塞尔的暴|政以及他把势力扩张到东部的计划。|我们的村庄是他们路上的第|一个聚居地。我不报仇誓不罢休。|不惜一切代价我也要找到阿克塞尔。
value.src: How could I ever doubt the poor creature? She was frightened and looking for help. Lisa told me about Axel Argen’s  tyranny and his plans to spread his influence to the east. My village was the first settlement on their way. I won’t rest until I have my revenge. I’ll get Axel, whatever it takes.

value.cn: 雇佣兵走的是靠近阿斯加德的隧道。|我敢说当地人和匪徒有勾结，|从军火走私里分一杯羹。
value.src: The mercenaries use the tunnel, which starts near Asgard. I bet locals cooperate with the bandits and get their interest from arms traffic.

value.cn: 我拿到了隧道门的钥匙，|开了几个小时后发现自|己到了一个陌生的地方。
value.src: I got the key to the tunnel door and after several hours’ driving I found myself in a strange place.

value.cn: 这里的人远不如我们村的文明。|不过我从他们那里打|听到了一些有趣的事：|丽莎是阿克塞尔的助手。|阿克塞尔是一个盘踞在阿尔|根的帮派头目。|这个帮派叫"|猩红之晨"，|听起来很危险。他们已向利|布里姆宣战，而这只是他们野|心勃勃计划的一部分。|我不太确定自己能否独|自对抗他们所有人。
value.src: The people here are far less civilized than my fellow-villagers. However, I learned some interesting things from them: that Lisa is Axel’s assistant. Axel is the leader of a gang based in Argen. |The gang is called ‘Scarlet Dawn’, and they sound dangerous. They’ve declared war against Librium and that’s just a part of their ambitious plans. I’m not so sure I can fight against them all on my own.

value.cn: 这里的人远不如我们村的文明。|也许这样反而好：|我更容易悄悄接近阿克塞尔。|原来这里也有政府，|正在和邻邦交战。|问题是阿克塞尔就是那个邻|邦的领袖，显然戒备森严。|我得动动脑筋才能接近他。
value.src: The people here are far less civilized than my fellow-villagers. Probably just as well: it will be easier to get to Axel unnoticed.|Turns out they have a government here, which is at war with the neighbor state. The trouble is, Axel is the leader of that state and is obviously well-guarded. I’ll have to use my brain to get to him.

value.cn: 我加入了独立城镇联邦——|利布里姆人这样称呼自己。|我觉得他们在为崇高的事业而战。|再说我们有共同的敌人——|阿克塞尔。
value.src: I joined the CIT, the Commonwealth of Independent Towns – that’s what Librium people call themselves. I think they are fighting for a noble cause. Besides, we have a common enemy. Axel.

value.cn: 接近阿克塞尔的最好办法大|概是加入他的猩红之晨军队。|我会赢得指挥官的信任，|获得引荐的机会。|那将是我除掉阿克塞尔的机会。
value.src: The best way to get to Axel is probably to join his Scarlet Dawn Army. I’ll gain the commander’s respect and get presented for reward. That’ll be my chance to kill Axel.

value.cn: 那真是一场地狱般的战争。|虽不总是正面交锋，|却始终充满破坏。|我不得不做了一些日后可能|会后悔的事。但现在阿克塞|尔已在我手中，我顾不上那些了。
value.src: That was a hell of a war. It wasn’t always direct, but it was always destructive. And I had to do things I’m probably going to regret. But I don’t have time for that now that Axel is in my hands.

value.cn: 击败猩红之晨的领袖后我大失所望。|我本以为会遇到一个野蛮的杀人魔，|但实际看到的却是一个有教养的、|关心人类未来的人。|虽然我无法认同他的方法，|但我有点喜欢他。|再说丽莎加在他头上的那些|罪名并不全是他的错。|原来她骗了我们俩。|她要为此付出代价。
value.src: I had a major disappointment after I defeated the Scarlet Dawn leader. I expected to meet a barbarian and a cruel murderer, but I actually saw an educated man, who’s concerned about the future of the humankind. And even though I couldn’t accept his methods, I sort of liked him. Besides, he wasn’t to blame for all those crimes Lisa accused him of. Turns out she fooled both of us. She’ll pay for it.

value.cn: 击败猩红之晨的领袖后我大失所望。|我本以为会遇到一个野蛮的杀人魔，|但实际看到的却是一个有教养的、|关心人类未来的人。|虽然我无法认同他的方法，|但我有点喜欢他。|原来丽莎一直瞒着他她的所作所为。
value.src: I had a major disappointment after I defeated the Scarlet Dawn leader. I expected to meet a barbarian and a cruel murderer, but I actually saw an educated man, who’s concerned about the future of the humankind. Even though I couldn’t accept his methods, I sort of liked him. It turned out Lisa kept him in the dark about her actions.

value.cn: 有了「解放者」的名声，|我只需向对的人打听，|就有人告诉我去哪里找丽莎。|她一看到我就跳上卡车，|直到意识到她的卡车远不|是我的对手，才不得不服|软并同意回答我的问题。
value.src: With my reputation of the liberator all I had to do was ask the right people and they told me where to look for Lisa. She jumped into her truck as soon as she saw me, and it was only when she realized that her truck was no match against mine, that she gave in and agreed to answer my questions.

value.cn: 既然我成了利布里姆的英雄，|追踪丽莎就不难了。|原来她在寻找失踪多年的著|名探险家伊万·戈。|她的调查将她引到了我的家乡，|但为时已晚：有人从死亡沙漠来，|销毁了所有证据。
value.src: Now that I became a hero of Librium, it wasn’t hard to track Lisa down and talk to her. It turned out, that she was looking for Ivan Go, the famous explorer, who’s gone missing many years ago. Her investigation led her to my native village, but it was too late: some people came from the Death Desert and destroyed all evidence.

value.cn: 即使走到天涯海角我也要找到凶手。|但没人能在死亡沙漠中活着回来。|据说北方岛屿的神谕知道所有|问题的答案，所以我和丽莎|要去拜访它。是的，她加入了队伍，|还带着一张关于伊万·戈重|要信息的光盘。丽莎在想办|法读取它，但至今没有成功。
value.src: I’m gonna get the murderers even if I have to go to the edge of the world for them. But no one has ever survived in the Death Desert before. They say that the Northern Isle Oracle knows answers to all questions, so we’ll visit it with Lisa. Yes, she’s joined me and she’s got a disc with important information about Ivan Go. Lisa is looking for a way to read it, but with no luck so far.

value.cn: 米德加德的工匠们同意为我制|造装置，但他们需要一些特定工具。|工具不难找，很快我就有一|辆能在沙漠中行驶的卡车了。
value.src: Midgard masters agreed to make the device for me, but they needed certain tools for it. They weren’t hard to find and soon enough I had a truck that could travel in the desert.

value.cn: 我的喜悦没持续多久。|丽莎偷走了两张光盘和海门钥匙！|她的踪迹通向西方。|我要追上她，问清楚为什么|要拿走这些只对我有价值的东西。
value.src: My joy didn’t last. Lisa has stolen both discs and the key to the Sea Gates! Her tracks lead to the West. I’ll follow her and ask her why she took the objects that had no value to anyone but me.

value.cn: 在去海门的路上我遇到了前所未|闻的怪物。差点被它们的守卫压碎，|但最终我摧毁了它！
value.src: I've never heard about the monsters I faced today on the way to the Sea Gates. I was this close to getting smashed by their guard, but in the end I destroyed it!

value.cn: 到达海滩时我一眼就看到了海门。|它是一座位于坚硬地面边|缘的宏伟建筑。我走近它，|把护符举过头顶——|护符莫名变得温暖起来。|下一刻我看见一条巨鱼浮出水面。|它张开了足以容纳两辆卡车的大嘴，|然后定格不动，仿佛邀请我开进去。|我心惊胆战地开了进去……|鱼嘴合拢，我听到巨响——|怪物潜回了深海。|这怪物原来是一台巨大机构，|和我的卡车一样。
value.src: When I reached the beach I saw the Sea Gates at once. It’s a grand construction on the edge of the firm ground. I approached it and lifted the Charm above my head, which felt warmer for some reason. The next thing I saw was a giant fish coming to the surface. The fish opened its mouth which looked big enough for two trucks to fit in, and froze as if inviting me to drive in. Terrified, I drove inside… The mouth closed and I heard a loud splash as the monster dived back into the sea depths.|The monster turned out to be a huge mechanism, like my truck.

value.cn: 这片地区真是异域风情：|巨大的树木和潮湿的空气唤|醒了我的原始本能。
value.src: The region was truly exotic: huge trees and humid air stirred primal instincts in me.

value.cn: 穿过丛林的唯一道|路把我引到了一个小聚居地。|当地人一看到我就开火，|我只好折返，寻找更热情的村庄。|幸运的是我很快就找到了。|另一个村庄的人热情地欢迎了我，|并提议结盟对抗好斗的德鲁伊。
value.src: The only road through the jungle led me to a small settlement. The locals opened fire at me the moment they saw me, so I had to turn back and look for a more hospitable village.| Luckily, I found it soon enough. The people of the other village gave me a warm welcome and offered an alliance against the aggressive Druids.

value.cn: 我不喜欢埋伏的主意，|但还是答应了帮助村民。|作为回报，机器崇拜者为我指|明了通往神谕的路。
value.src: I didn’t like the idea of an ambush, but I agreed to help the villagers nonetheless. In return for my help, the Machine-cultists showed me the way to the Oracle.

value.cn: 我拒绝参与他们的血腥计划，|于是朝森林之都——塞斯进发。
value.src: I refused to take part in their bloody plan, so I headed towards the forest capital – Seth.

value.cn: 穿过丛林的唯一道|路把我引到了一个小聚居地。|当地人一开始相当敌对，|但最终我们说清楚了。|原来只有塞斯的大德鲁伊知|道通往神谕的路，|于是我向塞斯出发。
value.src: The only road through the jungle led me to a small settlement. The locals were rather hostile to begin with, but we sorted it out in the end. It turns out that only the High Druid from Seth knows the way to the Oracle, so I set off towards Seth.

value.cn: 大德鲁伊给我出了道难题，|但几个钢铁怪物挡不住我。|不过完成他的任务并打听到神|谕的位置还是花了我一些时间。
value.src: The High Druid set a difficult task for me, but a few steel monsters couldn’t stop me. However, it took me a while to complete his task and learn the Oracle’s location.

value.cn: 说起神谕时，我以为会看到山|顶上的隐士小屋，|但眼前的一切与巫师和圣|人的传说截然不同……|那是一组通过通道连接的塔楼，|散发着能量。一个怪|物被过去的战士关在金色笼子里。|我就是这样第一次见到神谕的。
value.src: When we talked about the Oracle, I expected to see a hermit’s hut at the top of the mountain, but what I saw was so different from the stories about wizards and sages… It was a bunch of towers linked by passages, emitting energy. A monster was confined inside the golden cage by the warriors of the past. That’s how I first met the Oracle.

value.cn: 神谕要求我帮个忙作为交换|信息的代价。我无法拒绝。
value.src: The Oracle asked for a favor in return for information. I couldn’t but agree.

value.cn: 神谕同意读光盘，|条件是我完成某些仪式。|倒也公道，我想。|再说岛上到处是有趣的地方。
value.src: The Oracle agreed to read the disc if I carry out certain rituals. Fair enough, I thought. And besides, the island was full of interesting places.

value.cn: 当神谕接过光盘时我无比激动：|终于能听到父亲的信息了！|但当我听到神谕说"|请插入第二张光盘"|时，我彻底失望了！|可我只有一张！我立刻告诉了神谕，|差点忍不住破口大骂。|我简直不敢相信！|难道我所有的努力都白费了？|神谕面无表情地问我光盘从哪来的、|想用它查什么。他让我到父|亲遗物中去找第二张光盘。|我的第一反应是搜索父亲|留给我的旧卡车。
value.src: I was so excited when the Oracle took the disc: I was finally going to hear my father’s message! But I had a major disappointment when the Oracle announced: ‘Insert disc #2’! But I only had one! Of which I immediately informed the Oracle, barely able to keep from cursing. I couldn’t believe it! Were all my efforts vain? The Oracle asked me impassively where I got the disc from and what I was trying to find out with its help. He told me to look for the second disc among my father’s things. My first impulse was to search the old truck my father left me.

value.cn: 带着光盘和护符，|我再次拜访了神谕。|父亲的信息终于被解密了！|我终于听到了父亲的声音……|他说的是自己的生活和研究。|最重要的是，我知道了他曾|穿越沙漠寻找某个重要装置。|那一定是秘密的东西，|因为爸爸把日记藏得那么深。|我明白了爸爸想让我听到这些话，|知道他要去哪里——以防他回不来。|我必须找到他！
value.src: With the disc and the Charm in my bag, I visited the Oracle again. My father’s message was finally deciphered! At long last I heard my father’s voice… He was talking about his life and research. Most importantly I learned that he was traveling across the desert in search of an important device. It must have been something secret, since my dad hid his diary so well. I realized that my dad wanted me to hear these words and to know where he was heading, in case he couldn’t come back. I must find him!

value.cn: 穿过丛林的唯一道|路把我引到了一个小聚居地。|当地人热情地欢迎了我，|并提议结盟对抗好斗的德鲁伊。
value.src: The only road through the jungle led me to a small settlement. The locals gave me a warm welcome and offered an alliance against the aggressive Druids.

value.cn: 神谕无法解密丽莎的光盘，|但他告诉我有一种配件的设计图，|可以帮我穿越沙漠。
value.src: The Oracle couldn’t decipher Lisa’s disc, but he told me that there was a design of a gadget that could help me cross the desert.

value.cn: 两张光盘到手，我回到神|谕那里解密了伊万的日记。|我只需要集齐穿越沙漠所需的一切。
value.src: With both discs in my hands, I returned to the Oracle and deciphered Ivan’s diary. I just need to collect all the necessary things for traveling across the desert.

value.cn: 在烈日和风沙中开了几天车后，|我几乎不敢相信自己的眼睛——|我看到了奥西亚的土坯建筑。|你永远不知道这些人会怎样——|这一刻还友善，下一刻就想|捅你一刀。最奇怪的是他们对任|何问题都答非所问。|看起来他们失去了记忆。
value.src: After several day’s driving under the scorching sun and sandy wind, I could hardly believe my eyes when I saw the clay buildings of Oasia.|You never know what to expect from these people – now they are nice, the next moment they want to stab you in the back. And the strangest thing is that they can’t give coherent answers to any of my questions. It looks like they've lost their memory.

value.cn: 我打听到附近有一个记忆守|护者的村庄——他们这样称呼长老。|我得去那里找能帮我的人。|这里到底发生了什么……|这地方像是经历过一场大灾变。
value.src: I found out that there is a village of the Memory Keepers nearby – that’s what they call their elders. I’ve got to go there and find somebody who can help me. I wonder, what happened here… This place looks like it survived a major cataclysm.

value.cn: 我费了好大力气才找到通往守|护者村庄的路。那地方隐|藏在沙漠中的旧船之间，让我纳闷：|长老们在躲避谁？
value.src: With great difficulty I got the directions to the Keepers’ village. The place was well hidden in the desert among the old ships, which made me wonder: who are the elders hiding from?

value.cn: 我的到来在布哈拉居民中引|起了恐慌。直到记忆守护者|确信我没有恶意，|他们才告诉我悲惨的故事：|多年前某种神秘的疯狂攫|住了当地村民。他们开始互相残杀，|更糟的是事后对此毫无记忆。|不知为何布哈拉的长老们对这种|疯狂免疫，但他们一直生|活在被袭击的恐惧中。|让我震惊的是，并没有什么|神秘怪物，而是普通人在互相残杀、|毁坏自己的家园。
value.src: My visit caused panic among Bukhara population. It was only when the Memory Keepers realized that I didn’t mean harm that they told me their sad story:| Many years ago some mysterious madness seized the people of local villages. They started killing each other, and worst of all, they had no memory of what they had done afterwards. For some particular reason Bukhara elders were immune to that madness, but they lived in constant fear of an attack. It came as a shock to me that there were no mysterious monsters, but ordinary people were killing each other and destroying their own houses.

value.cn: 现在我明白了长老们为什么|如此努力地隐藏村庄。|我到后不久就有人开着坦克|来向布哈拉开火。|我不能让他们杀无辜的人！|我太清楚自己的村庄遭遇了什么。|我们战斗到摧毁最后一辆坦克，|然后帮助长老们坐船撤离。|作为回报他们告诉我，|有一个符合我父亲描述的人|曾经过他们的村庄，向东南方去了。|我要追上去！
value.src: Now I understood why the elders tried so hard to hide their village. People in tanks arrived soon after me and opened fire at Bukhara. I couldn’t let them kill innocent people! I remembered too well what happened to my own village. I fought until we destroyed the last tank and then helped to evacuate the elders on a ship. In return they told me that a man who fit the description of my father had once passed their village. He was heading the south-east. I’ll follow him!

value.cn: 丽莎的行为很反常：|莫名其妙地紧张，|最后竟然向我开始火。|这对我的耐心是极大的考验。|我意识到她不是叛徒，|只是这个地方对她的影响。|到达布哈拉时丽莎昏了过去，|我觉得她最好和前往大陆的长|老们在一起。本会照顾她的。|我继续寻找。
value.src: Lisa was acting really strange: she was nervous for no apparent reason and eventually opened fire at me. It was a major test for my patience. I realized that she was no traitor; it was just the effect the place had on her.| On arrival to Bukhara Lisa blacked out, so I thought she would be better off with the elders, who were heading to the main land. Ben will take care of her. I will continue my search.

value.cn: 我在沙中找到了一辆战斗中|严重受损的装甲卡车。|车里没有尸体，但我发现了一|件写着父亲名字的夹克。|他来过这里！看起来他弃车|步行继续了旅程。|我从车上取了几个配件——|太好了不该留在这里。|它们会成为父亲的纪念。|我确信我走对了路。
value.src: I found an armored truck in the sands, heavily damaged in combat. There was no body inside, but I found a jacket with my father’s name on it. He’s been there! Looks like he’s left the truck and continued his journey on foot.| I took a few gadgets from the car – they were too good to be left here. They will remind me of my father. I’m sure I’m on the right way now.

value.cn: 我对遭遇狂人军队毫无准备。|一群出乎意料的盟友|救了我免于一死。|沙漠深处那个科研聚居地|及其主人给我留下了奇怪的印象。
value.src: Nothing prepared me for the encounter with the army of madmen. I was saved from the imminent death by unexpected allies. Science settlement, lost in the middle of the desert, and its master made a strange impression on me.

value.cn: 翻过下一个沙丘，|我看到了可怕的一幕：|许多人围着一座巨大的金属|山纹丝不动。我说不清他们是|死是活。我不知道他们为何|聚集在此，但我感觉到伊万|·戈就在他们中间。|没有人回应我的呼喊和信号。|巨大的悲伤涌上心头。
value.src: Crossing the next dune, I saw a terrible sight: many people were standing motionless around a huge metal mountain. I couldn’t say whether they were dead or alive. I didn’t know why they gathered here but I felt, that Ivan Go was one of them. No one answered my cries and signals. The feeling of great sorrow came upon me.

value.cn: 我能感觉到从人圈中心传来的力量，|召唤我加入大多数人。|我设法抵抗并回到了聚居地。|在这里我了解到摧毁古代世|界的灾难及其原因。|人类不该玩弄超出自己理解|范围的东西！现在那台由科|学家启动的外星机构仍在运转，|毒害着我的星球。|一定有办法阻止这场疯狂。|伊万·戈似乎以前就在某处|见过外星机构。我应该和他的朋|友本·斯罗特尔谈谈。
value.src: I could feel the power coming from the center of the human circle, calling me to join the majority. I managed to resist it and return to the settlement. Here I learned about the catastrophe that destroyed the ancient world and its causes.  Humans should not play with the things beyond their understanding! Now the extraterrestrial mechanism, launched by the Scientist keeps working and poisoning my planet.| There must be a way to stop this madness. It seems that Ivan Go has already seen the alien mechanisms somewhere before. I should speak with his friend, Ben Throttle, about it.

value.cn: 我终于看清了真相。|邪恶的外星入侵者正用我在沙|漠中发现的那台巨大装置改|造我们的星球。但他们的主|基地在利布里姆一个叫塞|尔的城镇附近。其辐射干|扰了神谕的信号。|如果我摧毁基地，|我的机械盟友就能控制轨道|武器实施核打击，永远终结入侵！
value.src: My eyes are open. Evil alien invaders are terraforming our planet with the help of the huge device, I found in the desert. But their main base is somewhere around Seil, a town in the Librium. Its radiation jams the Oracle’s signals. If I destroy the base, my mechanical ally will take control over the orbital weapon and commit nuclear strikes that will stop the invasion for good!

value.cn: 我遇到了一个外星人，|他们自称涅里。现在我知|道过去到底发生了什么。|由于一系列不幸事件，|本应只在外太空运行的装|置在地球表面启动了。|它不断对地球和居民造成巨大伤害，|连涅里也无法靠近。|然而我去过那个地方并活了下来！|现在我的目标是将外星|人给我的几个装置安放在沙|漠飞船周围来阻止它。
value.src: I met one of the aliens, Njeri, as they call themselves. Now I now what really happened in the past. As a result of a series of unfortunate events, the device that was supposed to only work in outer space was turned on the surface of our planet. It constantly deals tremendous harm to the planet and its inhabitants and even Njeri cannot approach it. However, I visited that place and survived! Now my goal is to put several devices that the aliens gave me around the desert spaceship to stop it.

value.cn: 我能感觉到从人圈中心传来的力量，|召唤我加入大多数人。|我设法抵抗并回到了聚居地。|在这里我了解到摧毁古代世|界的灾难及其原因。|人类不该玩弄超出自己理解|范围的东西！现在那台由科|学家启动的外星机构仍在运转，|毒害着我的星球。|我必须连同其恐怖和秘密一|起摧毁这个地方。|神谕一定知道去哪里找到足|够强大的武器。
value.src: I could feel the power coming from the center of the human circle, calling me to join the majority. I managed to resist it and return to the settlement. Here I learned about the catastrophe that destroyed the ancient world and its causes.  Human should not play with the things beyond their understanding! Now the extraterrestrial mechanism, launched by the Scientist keeps working and poisoning my planet.| I must destroy this place along with its horrors and mysteries. The Oracle must know where to find a weapon powerful enough.

value.cn: 我没想到现实世界中|真的存在我今天见到的那种怪物。|通往神谕岛屿的路戒备森严，|但我成功击败了守卫！
value.src: I didn’t expect the monsters like the one I saw today exist in the real world. The path to the Oracle’s island was well guarded but I managed to defeat the Guardian!
